top.line: WSO2 Agent Manager as a partner: an open control plane for agents, and where behaviour policies plug in.
top.para: Generally available since 15 September 2026, it gives each agent an identity, runs every model and MCP call through an Envoy gateway with guardrails, hosts agents on Kubernetes with isolation tiers, and traces everything. The code is Apache 2.0; the supported build and support are paid. Behaviour policies add the mandate at the gateway, the kernel's enforcement in the runtime, and evidence in the same trace, shown by a five-step MVP.

in-short.line: An open control plane, aligned with our work; Apache 2.0 code; three places we add value; a five-step MVP.
in-short.para: And what we can learn from how it handles identity, isolation and inline policies.

post.line: Rania Khalaf's keel: it gives you speed with control; you go faster because of it.
post.para: The press release puts it as: speed and control get treated like a tradeoff, and they should not be.

what.line: Identity per agent per environment, an Envoy gateway on every call, Kubernetes isolation tiers, OpenTelemetry traces.
what.para: It supports LangGraph, CrewAI, Strands, Microsoft Agent Framework and A2A, with more than forty guardrails.

licence.line: The platform, gateway, policies, OpenChoreo and ThunderID are Apache 2.0, free to run in production.
licence.para: WSO2's signed images on its registry need a subscription for production, which brings updates and support; the newest release ships there first.

collaboration.line: Agent Manager knows who the agent is and what it called; it does not know what the agent is for.
collaboration.para: Behaviour policies add the mandate at the gateway, and the process layer below it that the gateway cannot see.

plug.line: The interceptor-service policy at the gateway, a SHarness runtime tier, and decisions as spans in the trace.
plug.para: The OPA policy sees only headers; runtime enforcement reaches only platform-hosted agents.

mvp.line: Quick start, a sample agent, a policy at the gateway, SHarness in the runtime, both in one trace.
mvp.para: No fork of WSO2's code; a design, not yet built.

learn.line: Identity per environment, isolation chosen per environment, policies inline on every call.
learn.para: And an honest limit: revoking a credential does not invalidate tokens already issued.

video.line: The highlights video in the post is WSO2's 'WSO2 Agent Manager is Live' on YouTube.
video.para: About a minute long; worth studying for how it explains a control plane in sixty seconds. Confirmed as the same video as the post's.

limits.line: The MVP is a design; WSO2 was not consulted; some pages read through a shortening tool.
limits.para: The 1.0.0 tag's commit date is later than the release date.

sources.line: WSO2's press release, docs, team page and code on GitHub, the LinkedIn post and the video.
